images.startAnchor: 217 vor Christus.
images.viewerTakeaway: Hannibal is trapped in a dangerous night situation, but the strange burning cattle hint at an unexpected solution.
images.visualPurpose: Hook and cover: establish the apparent trap, Hannibal and the bizarre fire deception in one instantly readable image.
images.topicAnchor: Hannibal during the 217 BCE escape from Fabius near the Falernian plain
images.visualConcept: Build one coherent night illustration with Hannibal large in the foreground near a blocked mountain pass, Roman silhouettes holding the heights in the distance, and a secondary connected ridge where burning brush bundles on cattle create moving points of fire; the image should tease the solution without explaining every step.
images.dominantSubject: Hannibal facing the blocked pass while the mysterious moving fire appears on the neighboring ridge
images.actionState: he studies the Roman-held route as the first strange fire points begin to move in the darkness
images.composition: place Hannibal and the blocked pass as the main foreground-to-midground axis, keep the Roman-held heights above the pass, and use the fire-bearing cattle as a smaller but bright secondary movement on the right ridge with clear negative space for the title
images.camera: a wide slightly elevated three-quarter night view that keeps Hannibal readable while showing the pass and neighboring ridge
images.depthPlan: foreground: Hannibal and a few Carthaginian guards; midground: narrow Roman-controlled pass; background/right ridge: moving fire points from the cattle
images.lightingMood: deep blue-black night with restrained moonlight and small warm orange fire accents, tense and mysterious rather than spectacular
supportingElements: Roman guards silhouetted at the pass
a few cattle carrying small burning brush bundles
images.continuityNote: Establish the pass, adjacent ridge and Hannibal's deep red cloak as recurring visual anchors for later scenes.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Use plausible 3rd-century BCE Carthaginian and Roman equipment; the fire comes from brush bundles tied to cattle horns, not from the horns themselves.

images.startAnchor: Hannibal sitzt in Süditalien scheinbar in einer Falle.
images.viewerTakeaway: The geography itself is the problem: Hannibal's route out is constricted by Roman-controlled high ground.
images.visualPurpose: Orient the viewer spatially before the trick begins.
images.topicAnchor: Falernian plain and narrow mountain exit in southern Italy, 217 BCE
images.visualConcept: Show a hand-drawn unlabeled terrain-map view of a broad cultivated plain narrowing into a mountain passage, with the Carthaginian force compressed on the plain side and Roman positions controlling the exit and surrounding heights.
images.dominantSubject: the bottleneck between the broad plain and the narrow mountain passage
images.actionState: the Carthaginian route visually funnels toward a Roman-controlled choke point
images.composition: use the narrowing terrain itself as a strong funnel from lower-left broad plain to upper-right pass, with small opposing army masses placed only where needed to explain the trap
images.camera: a high oblique map-like terrain view without modern labels or diagram boxes
images.depthPlan: foreground: broad plain with compact Carthaginian column; midground: narrowing ground; background: steep pass and Roman positions on higher terrain
images.lightingMood: late-day muted earth colors with clear terrain separation and no dramatic glow
supportingElements: Roman guard positions on the heights
one road narrowing into the pass
images.continuityNote: Keep the same pass orientation and adjacent ridge for all later overview scenes.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Avoid modern borders, labels, roads or city graphics; show only a plausible simplified ancient landscape.

images.startAnchor: Vor ihm liegt ein enger Pass.
images.viewerTakeaway: The exit is physically narrow and easy to defend.
images.visualPurpose: Make the choke point feel dangerous and concrete.
images.topicAnchor: narrow mountain pass controlled by Roman forces
images.visualConcept: Look directly into the narrow rocky passage from the Carthaginian side, with steep slopes closing in and only a thin traversable route between them.
images.dominantSubject: the constricted mountain passage
images.actionState: the empty route looks exposed and difficult to cross under enemy observation
images.composition: center the narrow route as a compressed opening between two dark slopes, with only a few distant Roman silhouettes high above to prove control without turning the image into a battle scene
images.camera: a low wide view from the entrance of the pass looking inward
images.depthPlan: foreground: rough road and rocks; midground: tight passage; background: high ridge with tiny Roman sentries
images.lightingMood: cool late-evening light with the passage already falling into shadow
supportingElements: small Roman sentries on the ridge
images.continuityNote: Use the same rock shapes and pass silhouette in later empty-pass and breakthrough scenes.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: No medieval fortifications or permanent gate; the control comes from troops and terrain.

images.startAnchor: Auf den Höhen warten römische Soldaten.
images.viewerTakeaway: Roman soldiers hold the high ground and can observe the passage below.
images.visualPurpose: Humanize the blocking force.
images.topicAnchor: Roman guards on high ground above Hannibal's escape route
images.visualConcept: Show a small Roman detachment on the ridge edge watching the darkening pass below, shields grounded and attention fixed on the route.
images.dominantSubject: the Roman guards confidently holding the ridge above the pass
images.actionState: they watch the route below from a strong defensive position and expect Hannibal to come through it
images.composition: place three Roman soldiers large on the ridge foreground with the pass dropping away behind and below them, keeping their visual control of the terrain obvious
images.camera: a medium-wide side view slightly below ridge level
images.depthPlan: foreground: Roman guards with shields; midground: ridge edge; background: pass and plain far below
images.lightingMood: last cool daylight with calm disciplined tension
images.continuityNote: Keep Roman shield colors and ridge terrain consistent when these guards react to the fires later.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Use plausible Republican Roman military equipment for 217 BCE, not later imperial armor.

images.startAnchor: Und Hannibal schleppt auch noch riesige Beute mit sich herum.
images.viewerTakeaway: Hannibal is not trying to escape with a light raiding party; he has a slow, burdened column and captured livestock.
images.visualPurpose: Show why simply slipping away is difficult.
images.topicAnchor: Carthaginian baggage, captured livestock and spoils during the 217 BCE campaign
images.visualConcept: Make a dense but readable cluster of captured cattle, loaded pack animals and baggage bundles the main subject, with Carthaginian soldiers managing the slow-moving spoils.
images.dominantSubject: the cumbersome mass of captured livestock and baggage
images.actionState: the baggage train is packed and slow, making a clean rapid escape through hostile terrain difficult
images.composition: fill the lower frame with cattle backs, packs and carts moving in one direction, while keeping only a few soldiers for scale and a distant pass to connect the problem
images.camera: a medium-wide low three-quarter view close to the baggage train
images.depthPlan: foreground: cattle and loaded packs; midground: soldiers guiding the column; background: darkening mountains
images.lightingMood: dusty dusk with subdued browns and olive tones
images.continuityNote: Reuse the same brown cattle and baggage design in the later breakthrough column.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Avoid modern wagons or equipment; keep loads simple and ancient-period plausible.

images.startAnchor: Ein Frontalangriff wäre genau das, was Fabius will.
images.viewerTakeaway: Attacking straight through the pass would mean fighting uphill into prepared Roman positions.
images.visualPurpose: Explain why brute force is the wrong option.
images.topicAnchor: Hannibal considering a frontal assault against the Roman-held pass
images.visualConcept: Create one readable tactical contrast: on the left, a compressed Carthaginian assault route climbs into Roman-controlled high ground; on the right, Hannibal stands apart looking toward the nearby cattle instead of committing troops to that route.
images.dominantSubject: the contrast between the dangerous frontal route and Hannibal choosing not to take it
images.actionState: the obvious military option is visibly costly while Hannibal's attention shifts toward an unconventional resource
images.composition: use the blocked uphill route as the larger left-side danger and Hannibal with the cattle as the smaller right-side alternative, keeping both comparison poles visible in one landscape
images.camera: a wide elevated tactical view with readable human scale
images.depthPlan: foreground: Hannibal and cattle on the right; midground-left: compressed approach to the pass; background: Romans holding higher ground
images.lightingMood: dusk with fading light and controlled contrast between the dark pass and lighter open ground
images.continuityNote: Keep the same pass geometry and cattle appearance from earlier scenes.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Do not show an actual mass frontal attack occurring; this image explains the rejected option.

images.startAnchor: Also greift Hannibal zu etwas völlig anderem.
images.viewerTakeaway: Hannibal decides to turn ordinary captured livestock into a deception device.
images.visualPurpose: Reveal the beginning of the plan without yet showing the final illusion.
images.topicAnchor: Hannibal ordering preparations for the cattle deception
images.visualConcept: Show Hannibal giving a quiet nighttime preparation order to handlers beside a gathered group of cattle, pointing toward the adjacent ridge rather than the pass.
images.dominantSubject: Hannibal directing the unusual preparation around the cattle
images.actionState: he points toward the ridge while handlers begin separating the strongest animals from the herd
images.composition: place Hannibal and two handlers in the foreground triangle, cattle mass behind them, and the target ridge visible over Hannibal's pointing arm
images.camera: a medium-wide eye-level view close enough for gesture and intent to read
images.depthPlan: foreground: Hannibal and handlers; midground: selected cattle; background: dark ridge
images.lightingMood: early night with low camp-light accents and restrained shadows
images.continuityNote: Keep Hannibal's clothing, cattle color and ridge orientation identical to the established world.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Present Hannibal as a plausible Carthaginian commander without claiming an exact portrait likeness.

images.startAnchor: Er lässt ungefähr zweitausend kräftige Ochsen zusammentreiben.
images.viewerTakeaway: The trick is large-scale, not a handful of animals.
images.visualPurpose: Show the surprising scale of the preparation.
images.topicAnchor: roughly two thousand cattle selected for Hannibal's deception
images.visualConcept: Show a broad nighttime staging area filled with a large organized herd of cattle being gathered by small groups of handlers, using depth and repetition to imply roughly two thousand without drawing thousands of tiny animals.
images.dominantSubject: the unusually large gathered herd
images.actionState: handlers compress the herd into a controlled mass before the fire bundles are attached
images.composition: let repeated cattle silhouettes fill foreground and middle ground in layered rows, with handlers only at edges and a dark ridge beyond
images.camera: a high medium-wide view over the gathered herd
images.depthPlan: foreground: several large cattle; midground: layered herd mass; background: handlers and ridge
images.lightingMood: dark night with sparse low warm lamps, mostly cool muted tones
images.continuityNote: Do not make every animal individually detailed; preserve the same brown cattle family for later fire scenes.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Use the source number as approximate scale; avoid literal text or numeric labels.

images.startAnchor: An ihre Hörner werden Bündel aus trockenem Reisig gebunden.
images.viewerTakeaway: The deception depends on simple combustible bundles fixed to the animals' horns.
images.visualPurpose: Make the mechanism physically understandable.
images.topicAnchor: dry brush bundles being tied to cattle horns
images.visualConcept: Use a close object-focused view of careful hands fastening a compact dry brush bundle around the base area of an ox's horns with simple cord, before anything is lit.
images.dominantSubject: the unlit dry brush bundle secured to the ox's horns
images.actionState: a handler tightens the final cord while another unlit bundle waits nearby
images.composition: make the horn, cord and brush bundle large in the center-left foreground with the handler's hands visible and the animal's head calm but simplified
images.camera: a close three-quarter detail view
images.depthPlan: foreground: horn, cord, brush bundle and hands; midground: ox head; background: soft silhouettes of other prepared cattle
images.lightingMood: dim warm preparation light against a cool night background
images.continuityNote: Use the same bundle construction in every later burning-cattle scene.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: The combustible material is tied to the horns; do not depict the horn itself as burning.

images.startAnchor: Dann wartet er bis tief in die Nacht.
images.viewerTakeaway: Timing is part of the weapon: the trick only works when distance and darkness hide what the lights really are.
images.visualPurpose: Create suspense before ignition.
images.topicAnchor: Carthaginian force waiting in deep night before the deception
images.visualConcept: Show the same valley and ridge in near-total calm just before the signal: cattle clustered in darkness, the Roman-held pass barely visible, and no flames yet.
images.dominantSubject: the silent dark landscape moments before the deception begins
images.actionState: both armies hold position while the prepared cattle wait unseen below the ridge
images.composition: use large areas of darkness and negative space, with only faint silhouettes revealing cattle, ridge and pass
images.camera: a very wide static night establishing view
images.depthPlan: foreground: dark cattle silhouettes; midground: ridge; background: faint Roman pass position
images.lightingMood: deep cool night with minimal moonlight and almost no warm accents
images.continuityNote: This is the same exact terrain immediately before the fires ignite.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Avoid fantasy moonlight or modern torches; keep the scene plausibly dark.

images.startAnchor: Auf ein Signal werden die Bündel angezündet.
images.viewerTakeaway: The plan suddenly turns from preparation into action.
images.visualPurpose: Deliver the ignition beat as a sharp visual change.
images.topicAnchor: handlers lighting the brush bundles on the cattle
images.visualConcept: Show a tight sequence within one coherent scene: one handler touches flame to the first brush bundle, a second nearby bundle catches, and handlers immediately begin moving the cattle toward the ridge.
images.dominantSubject: the first brush bundle catching fire on an ox's horns
images.actionState: small flames spread from the ignition point as the prepared animals begin moving
images.composition: place the first ignition large in the foreground and let two progressively lit animals recede diagonally toward the ridge, creating a clear start-to-motion sequence
images.camera: a medium close low view following the diagonal movement
images.depthPlan: foreground: first ignition; midground: second lit bundle and handler; background: cattle beginning to move uphill
images.lightingMood: sudden warm fire against deep blue-black night, bright enough to read but not glossy or explosive
supportingElements: two additional cattle beginning to move
images.continuityNote: Use the exact brush-bundle construction from Bild 09 and terrain direction from Bild 10.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Keep flames localized to the attached brush bundles and avoid gore.

images.startAnchor: Plötzlich bewegen sich hunderte Feuerpunkte einen Berghang hinauf.
images.viewerTakeaway: From a distance, the hillside fills with moving lights that no longer read as individual animals.
images.visualPurpose: Create the central visual spectacle of the deception.
images.topicAnchor: burning cattle climbing the ridge at night
images.visualConcept: Show the dark ridge with dozens of small moving warm fire points spread across its slope, while cattle bodies remain mostly lost in darkness so the viewer understands why the lights could be misread from far away.
images.dominantSubject: the moving constellation of fire points climbing the ridge
images.actionState: the lights rise unevenly across the slope and create the impression of a large moving force
images.composition: use the dark diagonal ridge as the whole frame and distribute warm fire points in clustered lines moving upward, with no single animal dominating
images.camera: a distant wide night view from the Roman side
images.depthPlan: foreground: dark ridge base; midground: moving fire clusters; background: black sky and upper ridge
images.lightingMood: high contrast between small orange flames and a cool nearly black landscape
images.continuityNote: Keep the same ridge silhouette first established in the cover and map views.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: The fires are attached brush bundles; do not turn the scene into a forest inferno.

images.startAnchor: Aus der Entfernung sieht es aus, als würde dort eine ganze Armee mit Fackeln marschieren.
images.viewerTakeaway: The Roman interpretation, not the fire itself, is the real weapon.
images.visualPurpose: Show perception vs reality in one integrated storytelling image.
images.topicAnchor: Roman guards mistaking the burning cattle for a moving enemy force
images.visualConcept: Create one integrated Roman-view illustration: large Roman guards in the foreground look across the darkness at distant organized-looking fire points on the ridge, while a smaller naturally connected lower foreground glimpse reveals one actual ox with a burning brush bundle, exposing the mismatch between what the guards think they see and what is really there.
images.dominantSubject: the Roman guards misreading the moving lights as enemy troops
images.actionState: their attention locks onto the apparent torch-bearing force while the real source of the lights remains visually secondary but discoverable
images.composition: make the Roman viewpoint and distant fire formation the main continuous scene, then integrate one smaller close reality moment at the lower edge without hard panel borders or unrelated collage fragments
images.camera: an over-the-shoulder wide view from behind the Roman guards with a small close reality element embedded in the same visual flow
images.depthPlan: foreground: Roman guards and one small close glimpse of an ox below; midground: dark valley; background: ridge filled with moving fire points
images.lightingMood: tense cool night with warm moving lights as the only strong accents
supportingElements: one close reality glimpse of an ox with a fire bundle
images.continuityNote: Keep the Roman guards from Bild 04 recognizable and the cattle/fire construction consistent.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Do not depict a literal second army; the distant lights only create that impression.

images.startAnchor: Die römischen Soldaten am Pass reagieren.
images.viewerTakeaway: The deception succeeds only because the Roman guards act on the false interpretation.
images.visualPurpose: Move from illusion to decision.
images.topicAnchor: Roman guards reacting to the apparent enemy movement on the ridge
images.visualConcept: Show the same Roman ridge detachment abruptly turning away from the pass toward the moving fires, one soldier pointing urgently while the others lift shields and start moving.
images.dominantSubject: the Roman guards deciding to respond to the lights
images.actionState: their bodies pivot away from the pass and toward the ridge, converting uncertainty into movement
images.composition: place the pointing soldier large in the foreground with two others turning behind him, while the pass remains visibly unattended at the far edge of the frame
images.camera: a medium-wide ridge-level view
images.depthPlan: foreground: reacting Roman guards; midground: ridge path toward the fires; background: unattended pass edge
images.lightingMood: fire-lit tension with cool shadows and small reflected warm accents
supportingElements: moving fire points in the distance
images.continuityNote: Use the same soldiers, shield colors and ridge position from Bild 04.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Show disciplined but uncertain movement, not panicked modern behavior.

images.startAnchor: Sie verlassen ihre starke Stellung und bewegen sich auf die Feuer zu.
images.viewerTakeaway: The crucial tactical change is simple: the guarded choke point becomes empty.
images.visualPurpose: Show the Roman mistake in spatial terms.
images.topicAnchor: Roman detachment leaving the choke point to approach the burning ridge
images.visualConcept: Show one wide tactical scene where Roman soldiers move away from the narrow pass toward the fire-lit ridge, leaving the actual passage visibly empty behind them.
images.dominantSubject: the direct spatial relationship between the departing Roman detachment and the newly unguarded pass
images.actionState: Roman soldiers climb toward the lights while the choke point they were protecting is now open
images.composition: put the moving Roman group on the bright rightward slope and the empty dark pass as an equally readable consequence on the left, connected by their abandoned route
images.camera: a high wide tactical view
images.depthPlan: foreground: empty pass entrance; midground: departing Roman group; background: moving fires higher on the ridge
images.lightingMood: cool night with warm lights pulling the eye away from the dark open pass
images.continuityNote: Keep the pass silhouette identical to Bild 03 so the change from guarded to empty is immediate.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: The scene simplifies troop numbers for readability but preserves the tactical relationship described by Polybius.

images.startAnchor: Genau darauf hat Hannibal gewartet.
images.viewerTakeaway: Hannibal watches the Roman position empty and knows the deception has created the opening he needs.
images.visualPurpose: Give the protagonist a clear decision beat before the escape.
images.topicAnchor: Hannibal observing the emptied pass
images.visualConcept: Show Hannibal in the dark foreground watching the Roman silhouettes move away from the pass, then giving a restrained forward signal to his officers.
images.dominantSubject: Hannibal recognizing the opening and signaling the march
images.actionState: he sees the pass clear and raises one hand to send the column forward
images.composition: place Hannibal large at left foreground facing the now-open pass in the middle distance, with the departing Roman lights high on the opposite ridge
images.camera: a medium-wide over-the-shoulder three-quarter view
images.depthPlan: foreground: Hannibal and one officer; midground: open pass; background: Roman movement toward the fires
images.lightingMood: deep night with low reflected fire glow and controlled tension
images.continuityNote: Keep Hannibal's deep red cloak and the established pass orientation unchanged.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Do not invent dialogue or exaggerated gestures; use simple command posture.

images.startAnchor: Während die Römer versuchen zu verstehen, was auf dem Berg passiert
images.viewerTakeaway: The Romans are still occupied by the false threat while the real escape begins elsewhere.
images.visualPurpose: Create simultaneous tension between distraction and movement.
images.topicAnchor: Roman confusion on the ridge while Hannibal begins the escape
images.visualConcept: Build one continuous night landscape with the Roman guards clustered around the confusing fire-lit cattle high on the right ridge while, lower and farther left through the now-open pass, the first Carthaginian troops quietly begin moving out.
images.dominantSubject: the contrast between Roman attention on the false threat and the real Carthaginian movement through the pass
images.actionState: Romans hesitate around the lights as the first enemy column slips through the route they abandoned
images.composition: use one broad landscape with two causally linked zones: brighter Roman confusion high right and darker real escape low left, connected by the empty pass between them
images.camera: a very wide elevated night view
images.depthPlan: foreground-left: first Carthaginian movement; midground: empty pass; background-right: Romans near the fire-lit cattle
images.lightingMood: cool dark landscape with warm distraction lights concentrated away from the real escape
supportingElements: small Roman group near the fires
first Carthaginian troops entering the pass
images.continuityNote: Keep both ridge and pass geometry consistent with Bild 15.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Do not add fantasy explosions or a large battle; the strength of the moment is simultaneous misdirection.

images.startAnchor: setzt sich die eigentliche karthagische Armee in Bewegung.
images.viewerTakeaway: The real army now moves through the route the Romans were supposed to hold.
images.visualPurpose: Show the breakthrough beginning clearly.
images.topicAnchor: Carthaginian army entering the unguarded pass
images.visualConcept: Show Hannibal's organized column entering the narrow pass in darkness, with heavy infantry leading, cavalry and baggage following in depth while the guarding heights remain empty.
images.dominantSubject: the Carthaginian column flowing into the unguarded passage
images.actionState: the front of the army has entered the choke point while the rest of the column compresses behind it
images.composition: use the pass as a strong leading corridor from foreground army mass into the center of the frame, with empty high ground on both sides emphasizing the opening
images.camera: a high three-quarter wide view looking along the pass
images.depthPlan: foreground: dense column approach; midground: troops inside the pass; background: route opening beyond
images.lightingMood: very dark blue night with sparse low torchlight inside the column
images.continuityNote: Reuse baggage design from Bild 05 and exact pass silhouette from Bild 03.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Keep formations simplified and plausible; no imperial-era uniforms.

images.startAnchor: Schwere Infanterie, Reiter, Beute und Nachhut ziehen durch den nun offenen Engpass.
images.viewerTakeaway: Hannibal gets more than a few men out; the entire burdened force and its spoils move through the opening.
images.visualPurpose: Pay off the earlier baggage problem by showing the whole mixed column escaping.
images.topicAnchor: Carthaginian heavy infantry, cavalry, baggage and rear guard passing through the gorge
images.visualConcept: Use one long readable marching column through the pass, with heavy infantry already farther ahead, cavalry behind them, baggage and captured cattle in the center, and the rear guard just entering.
images.dominantSubject: the full mixed Carthaginian column successfully threading through the gorge
images.actionState: different parts of the force occupy successive depths of the same route, proving the escape is working at scale
images.composition: organize the column as a deep S-shaped line through the pass so each group is distinct without labels or separate panels
images.camera: a wide elevated view from above one side of the gorge
images.depthPlan: foreground: rear guard entering; midground: baggage and cavalry; background: heavy infantry exiting the far side
images.lightingMood: night beginning to soften toward pre-dawn gray, with restrained torch accents
images.continuityNote: Keep all recurring equipment and cattle consistent with previous scenes.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: Follow Polybius' broad marching order without pretending every small formation detail is known.

images.startAnchor: Erst als die Römer näher kommen, erkennen sie den Trick
images.viewerTakeaway: The apparent army dissolves into its real components only when the Romans get close enough.
images.visualPurpose: Reveal the deception from the Roman point of view.
images.topicAnchor: Roman soldiers discovering the burning cattle deception
images.visualConcept: Show Roman soldiers stopping abruptly at close range as one ox with a burning brush bundle crosses in front of them and more cattle scatter on the dark slope behind.
images.dominantSubject: the Roman soldiers realizing the moving lights are cattle rather than enemy troops
images.actionState: their forward movement stops as the nearest animal makes the deception unmistakable
images.composition: place the ox and its burning bundle large across the foreground with two Romans recoiling or halting behind it, while more fire-bearing cattle recede up the slope
images.camera: a medium-wide low three-quarter view at close range
images.depthPlan: foreground: ox with burning bundle; midground: stunned Roman guards; background: scattered cattle and fading fire points
images.lightingMood: harsh localized firelight against cool darkness, startling but non-graphic
images.continuityNote: Use the exact cattle bundle construction from Bild 09 and Roman guards from earlier ridge scenes.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: No gore; show distress and confusion without sensationalizing animal suffering.

images.startAnchor: Doch da ist es zu spät.
images.viewerTakeaway: By the time the trick is understood, Hannibal's force is already beyond the choke point; the real victory was forcing the Romans to move.
images.visualPurpose: Close the story and visually state the strategic lesson.
images.topicAnchor: Hannibal's army clear of the pass at dawn after the cattle deception
images.visualConcept: At pale dawn, show Hannibal's long column already beyond the pass on one side while the Roman guards return toward their abandoned position too late on the other, making the consequence of their earlier movement immediately visible.
images.dominantSubject: the irreversible separation between Hannibal's escaping army and the Romans returning too late
images.actionState: the Carthaginian column continues away into open country while the Romans reach an empty choke point behind it
images.composition: place the departing Carthaginian column as the strong forward movement into the brightening left background and the smaller returning Roman guards at the dark pass on the right, linked by the now-empty road
images.camera: a wide elevated dawn view that echoes the earlier map-like trap but with the outcome reversed
images.depthPlan: foreground-right: returning Roman guards at the empty pass; midground: open road; background-left: Hannibal's column moving into open country
images.lightingMood: pale gray-blue dawn with a restrained warm horizon, relief for the escaping column and frustration at the pass
supportingElements: faint extinguishing fire smoke on the ridge
images.continuityNote: Match the original pass and ridge exactly so the viewer can read how the tactical situation has reversed.
images.historicalAccuracyNote: End on the escape and deception result, not on an invented triumphal scene or dialogue.
